channel.description: Recent content in Communication on Best of AI

item.title: Constant Contact
item.description:
Constant Contact has been a staple of small business email marketing for a long time. Users build mailing lists, design emails from templates with a drag-and-drop editor, schedule campaigns, and track opens and clicks. It emphasizes ease of use and customer support, including phone and chat help, which appeals to owners who are not marketing specialists.

The product extends beyond email. Tools include SMS marketing, social media posting, landing pages, online surveys, and event registration, with automation for welcome series and follow-ups. AI features generate email copy and subject lines, suggest content ideas, and help build campaigns from a short brief, and an AI-driven website builder is part of the suite.

item.title: Flourish
item.description:
Flourish makes data storytelling accessible. Users upload a spreadsheet, pick a template such as a bar chart race, scatter plot, hierarchy, map, or scrolling story, and customize colors, labels, and animations. The result is an interactive graphic that can be embedded in a website or article, or exported as an image or video.

Its biggest draw is the library of templates, including formats that are hard to build by hand, like animated race charts and data-driven stories that change as the reader scrolls. Teams can set up brand themes, collaborate on projects, and update charts when data changes. Newsrooms and organizations use it to publish clear graphics quickly.

item.title: Mentimeter
item.description:
Mentimeter makes presentations interactive. You build slides with questions such as multiple choice polls, word clouds, rating scales, rankings, and open-ended questions, share a join code or QR code, and the audience responds from their phones. Results appear live on the screen, which turns a one-way talk into a conversation and gives quiet participants an easy way to contribute.

It suits a range of settings. Teachers use it to check understanding, trainers to energize workshops, and companies to run all-hands meetings and collect anonymous feedback. Features include quizzes with leaderboards, Q&A with upvoting, and templates, and you can import existing slides from PowerPoint or Google Slides. AI helps generate a presentation from a prompt, suggest questions, and summarize responses.

item.title: Prezi
item.description:
Prezi stands out for its zooming interface. Instead of a linear deck, you lay out ideas spatially on a big canvas and the presentation moves among them with motion, which gives viewers a sense of how topics relate and can make a talk feel more dynamic. The approach suits overview-and-detail stories and keeps attention better for some audiences than traditional slides.

The product line has expanded. Prezi Video overlays presentation content next to the speaker on video calls and recordings, Prezi Design creates interactive visual content, and the AI assistant generates presentations from a prompt, rewrites text, and builds structure. Templates, brand kits, and analytics help teams use it for sales, teaching, and training.

item.title: Trados Studio
item.description:
Trados is one of the best-known tools among professional translators. When translators work on a document, Trados breaks it into segments and checks a translation memory for matches from previous projects, offering exact and fuzzy matches so work is reused and terminology stays consistent. That improves speed and quality, especially on repetitive technical content, and lowers costs for clients who pay by new words.

The product has evolved with the technology. It integrates machine translation engines, including adaptive and neural options, and supports AI-assisted features for suggestions and quality checks. Trados Enterprise is a cloud version for teams and organizations, supporting collaboration, project management, and workflows with vendors, while the desktop Studio remains popular among freelancers and agencies.

item.title: Claude Slides
item.description:
Claude Slides makes decks from a conversation. You describe the audience and the point of the presentation, share notes or source files, and Claude produces a set of slides with an outline, text, and layout. You can then ask for changes, such as a different order, a tighter message, or new visuals, and edit individual slides directly.

The finished deck can be presented from within Claude or exported to PowerPoint or PDF for use elsewhere. Because it lives in the same place as the conversation, you can pull information from uploaded documents and revise based on feedback without switching tools. It sits alongside Claude’s other creation features, including Docs.

item.title: ConvertKit
item.description:
ConvertKit was designed for independent creators rather than traditional businesses. It makes it easy to build a list with forms and landing pages, tag subscribers by interest, and send newsletters and automated sequences. The company later renamed the product Kit, and the old name remains widely used.

Creator commerce is a major part. Users can sell digital products, paid newsletters, and subscriptions directly, with payments handled in the platform. A recommendation network lets creators promote each other’s newsletters, and automations route subscribers based on what they click. AI tools help draft emails and subject lines.

item.title: GetResponse
item.description:
GetResponse bundles several marketing tools. Users collect subscribers with forms and landing pages, send newsletters, and build automated workflows that respond to behavior such as signing up, clicking, or buying. A webinar feature lets businesses host live events and follow up with attendees.

AI helps create content. An assistant drafts emails, subject lines, and landing pages, and builds campaigns from a short brief, while segmentation and analytics help improve results. E-commerce features include product recommendations and abandoned cart emails, and integrations connect with online stores and CRMs.

item.title: Mailchimp
item.description:
Mailchimp is one of the best-known email marketing services. You build an audience list, design emails with a drag-and-drop editor or templates, and send campaigns with reporting on opens and clicks. Automations send welcome series, abandoned cart reminders, and birthday messages, and signup forms and landing pages help grow the list. It also supports basic CRM features, social posting, and simple websites.

AI is built into content and targeting. Generative tools help write subject lines and email text, and build designs from a brand’s assets. Predictive segmentation estimates customer behavior, such as likelihood to buy, and send-time optimization chooses delivery times. Intuit’s AI assistant brings help with questions about campaigns. Integrations connect with Shopify, WooCommerce, and hundreds of other apps.

item.title: MailerLite
item.description:
MailerLite offers the core tools of email marketing without clutter. Users build a list, design emails with a drag-and-drop editor, set up automations that respond to subscriber behavior, and publish landing pages and sign-up forms. Websites and simple stores can also be built within the platform.

Features include segmentation, A/B testing, an AI writing assistant, and e-commerce integrations with Shopify and WooCommerce. Analytics show opens, clicks, and revenue. Paid subscription newsletters are supported, which has drawn creators.

item.title: memoQ
item.description:
memoQ helps translators work faster and stay consistent. As a translator works through a document, the tool shows matches from a translation memory of earlier work and terms from a glossary, so repeated phrases are translated the same way. Machine translation can provide suggestions that the translator edits.

For teams, memoQ’s server and cloud products manage projects, assign work to translators and reviewers, and track deadlines and costs. It supports many file formats and quality checks, and integrates with machine translation engines and AI services, including large language models for suggestions and review.

item.title: Smartling
item.description:
Smartling connects content systems to translators. Websites, apps, and documents flow in through integrations, and Smartling applies translation memory and machine translation, then routes text to human linguists where quality matters most. Translations return to the source system.

Features include visual context for translators, glossaries, quality scoring, and AI that translates and edits at scale. The company has pushed AI-first workflows to reduce cost and time, and reports on translation quality and spend.

item.title: SYSTRAN
item.description:
SYSTRAN is among the oldest names in machine translation. Its modern products use neural models, offered as an API, a desktop app, and server software that can run inside an organization’s own network. This matters for sensitive documents.

Customization lets organizations tune translation to their terminology, and the platform handles many file formats and language pairs. Government and corporate customers use it for large volumes of content.

SYSTRAN is sold by subscription and license. General-purpose language models now compete in translation quality. Alternatives include DeepL, Google Cloud Translation, Microsoft Translator, Amazon Translate, and Lilt. SYSTRAN suits organizations needing private, deployable translation.

item.title: Warmbox
item.description:
Warmbox addresses a deliverability problem. New or little-used email accounts sending outreach often land in spam. Warmbox connects an account to a network of inboxes that exchange emails, open and reply to them, and gradually build a positive sending history.

It is used before and during cold email campaigns, with dashboards that show inbox placement and health. Settings control volume and ramp-up.

Warmbox is paid, with plans by mailboxes. Warm-up does not fix poor targeting or bad content, and spam laws still apply. Alternatives include Instantly, Smartlead, Lemwarm, Mailreach, and Warmup Inbox. Warmbox suits teams sending cold email.

item.title: Datawrapper
item.description:
Datawrapper was built by journalists for journalists. A user pastes or uploads data, chooses a chart type such as a bar, line, scatter plot, or map, and adjusts labels, colors, and annotations. The result is a responsive graphic that works on phones and desktops, and can be embedded in a story or exported as an image.

Its design defaults follow good data visualization practice, so charts look clear without fiddling. Features include color-blind friendly palettes, tables with inline bars, locator maps, and a way to update charts automatically from a linked data source. News organizations around the world use it, and teams can share themes to keep a consistent style.

item.title: ActiveCampaign AI
item.description:
ActiveCampaign is built around automation. You design customer journeys that react to behavior: someone joins a list, visits a page, abandons a cart, or opens an email, and the system sends the right follow-up at the right time. Segmentation, split testing, site tracking, and a built-in CRM let small and mid-sized businesses personalize campaigns without a large marketing team. It is common in e-commerce, services, and B2B companies.

Its AI tools help build and manage those journeys. Active Intelligence can audit an account, draft campaigns and automations from a short description, flag automations that are broken or underperforming, and answer questions about results in plain language. Predictive features estimate the best time to send, how likely a contact is to buy, and which deals are most likely to close. A content assistant writes subject lines and email copy.

item.title: Beautiful.ai
item.description:
Beautiful.ai tackles a common complaint about PowerPoint: you spend more time fiddling with alignment than thinking about content. Its slides are built from smart templates that rearrange themselves when you add or remove text, images, or chart elements, so the design stays clean. Rules keep spacing, fonts, and colors consistent, and a library of layouts covers timelines, comparisons, charts, team slides, and more.

AI features help create the first draft. You can describe a presentation, or paste in notes, and it generates an outline and slides in the app’s format, which you then edit. Teams can store brand colors, fonts, and logos in a shared theme, share slide libraries, and collaborate on decks with comments. Presentations can be exported to PowerPoint or PDF, or shared by link with view analytics.

item.title: Boomerang
item.description: Boomerang adds time management to Gmail and Outlook. You can write an email and schedule it to send later, set a message to return to your inbox if nobody replies by a certain date, or hide an email until the moment you want to deal with it. Recurring messages, read receipts, and a pause feature that holds incoming mail until you choose to see it help people manage busy inboxes.

item.title: Brevo AI
item.description:
Brevo started as an email marketing service called Sendinblue and has expanded into a broader customer engagement suite. It covers email and SMS campaigns, WhatsApp messaging, transactional email for apps, landing pages, forms, live chat, and a CRM for sales pipelines. Automation workflows send messages based on behavior, such as a signup or abandoned cart, and segmentation lets marketers target the right audience.

AI features support content and timing. A writing assistant drafts subject lines and email copy, generates images, and adjusts tone, while send-time optimization picks the best time to reach each contact. Predictive tools estimate engagement, and AI chat features help with customer conversations. The product is positioned for small and mid-sized businesses that want many channels in one tool at a reasonable price.

item.title: Canva
item.description: For infographics, Canva works as a template-first editor. You choose a layout for a process, timeline, comparison, statistic, or report, then replace the placeholder text and swap in your own colors and fonts. The element library supplies icons, illustrations, shapes, and photos, and chart tools let you paste or upload numbers to draw bar charts, pie charts, and other graphs that update when the data changes. Because it is a drag-and-drop tool, people without design training can produce something tidy in under an hour.

item.title: Decktopus
item.description: Decktopus is built for people who need a presentation quickly. You enter a topic or a short brief, answer a few questions about the audience and goal, and the AI produces an outline and a deck of designed slides with suggested images and speaker notes. You then edit the text and layout in a drag-and-drop editor. It also offers templates for pitches, reports, and sales decks, and a brand kit for colors and logos.

item.title: DeepL
item.description:
DeepL built its reputation on translations that read more naturally than many competitors, especially for European languages. You paste text or upload a document, such as a Word file, PDF, or PowerPoint, and get a translation that keeps the formatting. Options let you choose formal or informal tone, add glossaries for specific terms, and see alternative wordings for phrases.

The product has expanded into a broader language platform. DeepL Write improves and rephrases text in the same language, DeepL Voice translates live conversations and meetings, and browser extensions and desktop apps translate as you work. An API serves developers and enterprises, and newer agent features automate tasks. Business plans add data security, which promises that texts are not used for training, plus team glossaries.

item.title: Gamma
item.description:
Gamma reimagined the presentation. Instead of slides built from a blank template, you describe what you want, such as a pitch for a new product or a lesson on photosynthesis, and Gamma generates a complete, designed deck with text, layouts, and images. The format uses flexible cards that expand and collapse, so presentations can feel more like interactive documents, and it also produces documents and one-page websites.

Editing is conversational and visual. You can ask the AI to rewrite a section, change the style, add images, or restructure, or edit manually with simple controls. Themes keep designs consistent, brand settings apply company fonts and colors, and sharing by link includes analytics on who viewed it. Decks can be exported to PowerPoint or PDF, and it integrates with other tools.

item.title: Google Translate
item.description: Google Translate is the translation tool most people try first. You type or paste text and get a translation in a second, with the language detected automatically. The mobile app adds the features travelers rely on: a camera mode that replaces text on signs and menus, a conversation mode that translates both sides of a spoken exchange, handwriting input, and offline language packs that work without a connection. Chrome can translate whole web pages, and you can upload documents and get a translated copy.

item.title: Infogram
item.description:
Infogram helps turn numbers into visual stories. You choose a template for an infographic, report, chart, or dashboard, import data from a spreadsheet or connect to a live source, and customize the design with your brand colors and fonts. The tool produces polished charts and maps, many of them interactive, that can be embedded on websites or shared as links.

Several features support data communication. Over thirty chart types, including maps and tables, handle different kinds of data, and live data connections update visuals when the source changes. Teams can collaborate on projects, keep brand templates, and publish with analytics. Downloads include images and PDFs, and AI features help generate visuals and suggest ways to present data.

item.title: Klaviyo AI
item.description:
Klaviyo is built on the idea that a store’s own customer data is the best basis for marketing. It connects to platforms like Shopify, BigCommerce, and WooCommerce, pulling in orders, browsing behavior, and product information. Marketers build segments, such as customers who bought twice in the last 60 days, and send targeted email and SMS campaigns and automated flows, like abandoned cart reminders, welcome series, and post-purchase follow-ups.

AI adds prediction and automation. Klaviyo estimates a customer’s likelihood to buy again, expected lifetime value, and probable next order date, and uses those signals for segmentation. Product recommendations personalize emails, send-time optimization chooses delivery times, and generative tools write subject lines and campaign copy and build flows from a description. A customer hub, reviews, and a CDP add other parts of the retention workflow.

item.title: Lokalise AI
item.description:
Lokalise helps teams ship products in multiple languages. Developers and designers connect their code repositories and design files, and Lokalise collects the text that needs translating, lets translators and reviewers work on it in an editor with context, and sends finished translations back. Integrations with GitHub, GitLab, Figma, and content systems keep localization in step with development rather than delaying releases.

AI sits at the center of recent versions. It can translate new strings with models that take glossaries, tone, and context into account, flag likely errors, and score translation quality so humans focus on the content that needs attention. Translation memory reuses approved translations for consistency and cost savings, and workflows route content to in-house teams or translation vendors. Reporting shows progress by language.

item.title: Microsoft Translator
item.description:
Microsoft Translator covers the common translation needs. You can type or paste text, speak into a phone for conversation translation, translate images and documents, and use offline language packs when traveling. Multi-device conversation mode lets several people speak in different languages and see translations on their own screens, which suits meetings and travel.

It’s integrated throughout Microsoft products. Teams offers live captions and translated meetings, Office apps can translate documents and text, and Edge translates web pages. For developers and businesses, Azure AI Translator provides APIs for text, document, and speech translation, with custom models and glossaries, and options to run in containers.

item.title: Mixmax
item.description:
Mixmax turns Gmail into a sales workspace. It tracks opens, clicks, and replies, lets you schedule messages, and adds a calendar tool so recipients can book meetings from your email. Templates and snippets speed up repetitive writing, and polls, surveys, and documents can be embedded. It is used by sales, recruiting, and customer success teams that live in their inbox.

Sequences are a main feature: automated multi-step email campaigns that send follow-ups until someone replies, with rules for pausing and routing. Integrations connect with Salesforce, HubSpot, Outreach alternatives, Slack, and Zapier, so activity is logged in the CRM. AI helps draft emails, personalize at scale, and suggest next steps, and call recording and meeting notes have been added in some plans.

item.title: Phrase
item.description:
Phrase helps companies translate software and content into many languages. Developers connect repositories and design tools, and new text is sent to translators or machine translation, then returned to the product when approved. Translation memory reuses earlier work and glossaries keep terminology consistent.

The platform brings together several products that grew from a merger: a translation management system, a string management tool for software teams, and a computer-assisted translation editor. AI translation engines and quality estimation reduce the amount of human review needed for lower-risk content.

item.title: Piktochart
item.description: Piktochart is aimed at people who need to present information visually but are not designers. You choose a template for an infographic, report, presentation, or poster, edit the text and images, and add charts and maps that you can link to data. Visual blocks, icons, illustrations, and a library of graphics make it quick to produce clean results, and the tool exports to image and PDF formats or shares online.

item.title: Pitch
item.description:
Pitch aims to make presentations that look good without wrestling with layouts. It provides modern templates, smart slide types, and a brand-aware design system that keeps a team’s decks consistent. Collaboration works like a shared document: several people edit at once, leave comments, and track versions, which suits startups, agencies, and sales teams that produce decks together.

Distinctive features include presentation analytics and sharing. You can send a deck as a link and see who viewed it and for how long, which is helpful for investor and sales decks, and recordings let you narrate a deck for asynchronous sharing. AI tools generate slide drafts from a prompt, rewrite text, and create visuals, and the platform integrates with tools like Slack, HubSpot, and Google Drive.

item.title: Plus AI
item.description:
Plus AI takes the approach that you shouldn’t have to leave your slide editor to use AI. After installing the add-in in Google Slides or PowerPoint, you describe the presentation you want, and it drafts an outline and slides in the editor, which you can then adjust like any other deck. It can also build from a document, a set of notes, or a web page.

Editing features save time on existing decks. The remix tool can restyle or rework slides, and the rewrite function changes tone or length of text on a slide. It can convert content into a different layout, summarize, and create speaker notes. Because the output is native slides, the file remains fully editable and compatible with company templates and brand assets.

item.title: Reverso
item.description:
Reverso is known for context. Beyond a plain translation, it shows examples of the word or phrase used in real texts, such as books, subtitles, and documents, with the original and translation side by side. That helps learners and translators choose the right expression, understand nuance, and see how phrases are typically used in each language.

The product includes several tools. A translator handles text and documents, Reverso Context is the example search, and a grammar and spell checker works across languages. Verb conjugators, vocabulary lists, and flashcards support learning, and AI features paraphrase and improve text. Browser extensions and mobile apps make it available while reading or writing.

item.title: SaneBox
item.description:
SaneBox tackles inbox overload without replacing your email app. It connects to your existing account and analyzes your behavior, such as who you reply to and which messages you open, then moves less important mail into a folder called SaneLater. Newsletters, notifications, and cold outreach end up there, and you get a digest to skim when you choose. The important mail stays in your inbox.

Several tools help you stay in control. SaneBlackHole sends unwanted senders away permanently with a single drag, snooze folders let you hide a message until later, and reminders alert you if a recipient has not replied. A Do Not Disturb feature holds mail for a period. Because it works on the server, it functions with Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail, Yahoo, and other providers, and on all your devices.

item.title: Shortwave
item.description:
Shortwave is a Gmail client that rethinks the inbox. Related messages are grouped into threads, newsletters and receipts can be bundled so they do not clutter the main view, and snooze, scheduling, and split inboxes help you process email faster. It works on Mac, Windows, iOS, Android, and the web, and connects to your Gmail account.

AI is central. You can ask the assistant questions about your email, such as what a client asked for last month or when a trip was booked, and it searches and answers using your messages. It summarizes long threads, drafts replies in your tone, and can take actions like organizing, labeling, and scheduling. The goal is to cut the time spent finding and writing.

item.title: Slidebean
item.description:
Slidebean separates writing from design. You enter text for each slide in an outline-style editor, choose a slide type such as problem, solution, market, or team, and the software lays it out, selecting fonts, spacing, and graphics so the result looks professional. That means founders can focus on the message and avoid spending hours on layout. AI features help draft slide content and improve wording.

Because it was built for startups, Slidebean adds extras beyond slides. It offers pitch deck templates based on successful funding decks, tools to share decks and see who viewed them, and a financial model builder for projections. The company has also offered pitch deck design and fundraising services for founders who want expert help.

item.title: SlidesAI
item.description:
SlidesAI works inside Google Slides. You paste in text, such as an essay, notes, or an article, or enter a topic, and the add-on creates a set of slides with titles, bullet points, and layout. It lets you pick a presentation style, color theme, and the number of slides, and can add relevant images. The result is a draft that you edit like any other Google Slides deck.

Additional features support content work. It can summarize long text into key points, paraphrase for clarity, and generate text for slides from a prompt. Because the output is a native Slides file, it can be shared, collaborated on, and presented as usual. It’s popular with students, teachers, and professionals who need a quick starting point.

item.title: Smartcat
item.description:
Smartcat brings machine and human translation together. A company uploads documents or connects content sources, receives AI translation immediately, and can request human review from freelance linguists or agencies in its marketplace, all with translation memory and glossaries.

Workflow tools manage projects, deadlines, and payments, and the platform supports many file types and integrations. AI agents handle tasks such as quality checks, and the pricing model aims to keep costs lower than traditional agencies.

item.title: Spark Mail
item.description:
Spark is an email client that works with Gmail, Outlook, iCloud, Yahoo, and other accounts. Its Smart Inbox sorts messages into categories, putting people and important mail first and keeping newsletters and notifications out of the way. Features such as snooze, send later, follow-up reminders, and quick replies make it faster to process mail, and a unified inbox combines accounts.

Collaboration is a differentiator. Teams can share emails, comment privately on messages, and draft replies together before sending, which suits small teams who handle shared mailboxes. AI features in the paid tier help write and rewrite emails, summarize long threads, and suggest replies, and a feature can search by asking questions. The app is available on Apple devices, Android, and Windows.

item.title: Superhuman
item.description:
Superhuman became known as the fastest email client. It’s designed so you can process your inbox with the keyboard, using commands for archiving, replying, snoozing, and reminders, and everything loads instantly. The interface is minimal, with Split Inbox sections that separate important mail from newsletters and notifications. Features such as send later, follow-up reminders, read statuses, and a command palette are built into the workflow.

AI is now part of the experience. It drafts replies in your voice, summarizes long threads, searches your mail in plain language, and can write emails from short prompts. The company that owns Superhuman acquired it, changed its own name to Superhuman, and groups it with Grammarly’s writing assistant and the Coda workspace in a combined suite.

item.title: Tome
item.description:
Tome became a popular early example of generative AI for presentations. A user described a topic, and Tome produced a complete, designed narrative with text, images, and layout, which could be edited in a flexible, canvas-like format. It was positioned as a more modern, storytelling-focused alternative to PowerPoint, and gained millions of users, with attention from students, founders, and professionals.

The company later decided to retire the presentation product and pivot to something different, a sales-focused application. Users were given a period to export their work before the service closed. The pivot reflected a challenge facing many AI tools: general features are quickly matched by larger products, and a standalone app needs a defensible niche.

item.title: Venngage
item.description:
Venngage targets people who need to communicate information visually. Users start from thousands of templates for infographics, reports, flyers, presentations, and social graphics, replace the content, and customize colors, icons, and charts. Data can be imported to generate charts, and the tool includes maps and diagrams for explaining processes and comparisons.

It differentiates itself with business features. Brand kits apply logos, fonts, and colors automatically, team workspaces allow collaboration and approvals, and an accessibility checker flags color contrast and other issues. AI tools generate infographic designs from text, write copy, and suggest improvements, and designs can be exported or shared with analytics.

item.title: Visme AI
item.description:
Visme is aimed at people who need to present information visually without design skills. It offers a drag-and-drop editor with thousands of templates for presentations, infographics, reports, charts, social media posts, and documents. Data widgets create charts and graphs from spreadsheets, and interactive elements such as links and animations can be added. Brand kits keep colors, fonts, and logos consistent across a team.

AI features speed up creation. An AI designer can generate a presentation or document from a prompt, write and rewrite text, create images, and suggest layouts. Teams can collaborate in real time with comments and workflows, and content can be exported as PDF, PowerPoint, or HTML, or shared by link with analytics. Visme is often used by marketers, educators, consultants, and communications teams.

item.title: Spike
item.description:
Spike presents email like a chat. Threads become conversations, which can feel faster, and a unified view combines email with notes, tasks, and calendar. Teams can discuss messages privately without forwarding.

AI helps with summaries of long threads, drafting replies, and organizing the inbox, and shared inboxes support small teams. It works with many email providers.

Spike has a free tier and paid plans. Chat-style email is a taste, and some prefer traditional layouts. Alternatives include Superhuman, Shortwave, Hey, Gmail with Gemini, and Front. Spike suits people who want a conversational inbox.

item.title: MagicSlides
item.description:
MagicSlides speeds up deck creation. A user enters a topic, pastes text, or uploads a document, and the tool builds slides with titles, bullets, and images. Because it works as an add-on inside Google Slides and PowerPoint, the results land in a familiar editor for refinement.

It supports many languages and offers themes and layouts. Students use it for assignments, and professionals use it to produce a first draft of a presentation, which they then edit. Images can be sourced automatically.
